extracted.intended_audience: researchers reporting in vivo/preclinical animal experiments (authors of manuscripts using animals)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for how to report design, conduct and analysis of in vivo (animal) experiments to maximise reproducibility and reduce bias, covering exclusions, sample sizes (n), randomisation, blinding, outcome measures, and statistical methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions and outliers (explicit reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accompanying information should include an explicit description of whether researchers were blinded to the group allocations when data or animals were excluded. Explicitly state where built-in models in statistics packages have been used to remove outliers (e.g. GraphPad Prism’s outlier test).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report reasons for excluding animals or data points (e.g. illness, mortality, biologically implausible values). State whether exclusions occurred blinded to treatment allocation. If outliers were removed using software tests or built-in models, name the test/algorithm and the rule used (e.g. Cook’s D > 0.5). Provide examples and justify exclusions so readers can assess potential bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3c For each analysis, report the exact value of n in each experimental group
rubrics_metrics.description: The exact number of experimental units analysed in each group (i.e. the n number) is essential information for the reader to interpret the analysis; it should be reported unambiguously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report absolute numbers for each outcome (e.g. 10/20, not 50%). Account for all animals and data used in the experiment. For studies measuring animals at different time points, explicitly report which animals underwent which measurements and when. Report losses and excluded animals with reasons so readers can follow the flow from allocation to analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4a State whether randomisation was used and provide the method
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether randomisation was used to allocate experimental units to control and treatment groups. If done, provide the method used to generate the randomisation sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the type of randomisation used (simple, stratified, randomised complete blocks, minimisation, etc.), the method used to generate the sequence (e.g. computer-generated, RAND() in Excel, online random number generator), and what was randomised (treatment to experimental unit, order of treatment, etc.). If randomisation was not used, state this explicitly and explain how groups were formed. Explain allocation concealment where relevant. Use validated randomisation methods to minimise selection bias and consider allocation concealment to prevent deciphering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations for the randomisation strategy (blocking, stratification, minimisation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on selecting an appropriate randomisation strategy: simple randomisation, randomisation within blocks, stratified randomisation, and minimisation are described and contrasted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple randomisation may lead to imbalance and is rarely appropriate alone. Blocking controls known nuisance variables by randomising within blocks (e.g. cage, day), stratification groups by traits likely related to outcome (e.g. weight class), and minimisation balances multiple factors dynamically. List nuisance variables considered (time/day, litter, cage/tank, investigator, equipment, baseline measurements, animal characteristics, location) and ensure blocking factors are included in the analysis (blocking uses degrees of freedom). Choose a strategy appropriate to sample size and potential confounders; describe implementation in detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4b Strategy to minimise potential confounders
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the strategy used to minimise potential confounders such as the order of treatments and measurements, or animal/cage location. If confounders were not controlled, state this explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report steps to ensure no systematic differences between groups aside from treatment (standardisation, randomising sampling/measurement order, blocking, counterbalancing). If constraints prevent randomisation, explain how nuisance variables were accounted for in the analysis (see Statistical methods). Give concrete examples (e.g. randomising testing order daily, blocking by body weight) and cite reasons when no measures were used.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5 Blinding (who was aware at each stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe who was aware of the group allocation at the different stages of the experiment (during the allocation, the conduct of the experiment, the outcome assessment, and the data analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report blinding/allocation concealment at each stage: allocation (concealment until assignment), conduct (animal care staff/treatment administrators blinded where possible), outcome assessment (collectors/assessors blinded, randomise order of examination; if impossible use automated or third-party analysis), and data analysis (analyst blinded to which treatment corresponds to which group; code data prior to analysis). If blinding was not possible at any stage, state this and justify (e.g. overt phenotype), and describe partial mitigation strategies. Explain roles/people who were and were not blinded.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6a Clearly define all outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define all outcome measures assessed (e.g. cell death, molecular markers, or behavioural changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly describe what was measured and how (operational definitions). Specify units and measurement methods; choose unbiased recording (e.g. blinded assessment, automated tracking) where possible. Explain relevance of each outcome to study objectives. Avoid ambiguity where measures could be operationalised in different ways (e.g. activity as time moving vs distance travelled).

rubrics_metrics.name: 6b Identify primary outcome for hypothesis-testing studies
rubrics_metrics.description: For hypothesis-testing studies, specify the primary outcome measure, i.e. the outcome measure that was used to determine the sample size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which outcome is primary and whether it was defined prior to data collection and used for sample size calculation. If no primary outcome was pre-specified (exploratory studies may have multiple outcomes), explicitly state so. Registering a protocol in advance is recommended to avoid selective outcome reporting (primary outcome switching). Note that secondary outcomes may be underpowered if sample size is based on the primary outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7a Provide details of statistical methods used for each analysis, including software
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details of the statistical methods used for each analysis, including software used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide statistical methods a priori (see protocol registration). Report the specific tests/analyses used for each outcome, any data transformations, handling of missing data and outliers, and the software and version used. Distinguish between descriptive and inferential analyses and justify chosen methods with respect to study design. Specify treatment of blocking factors or covariates in models and any multiple-comparisons adjustments.
